title: History · People and ideas
summary: 161 researched historical portrait episodes covering 140 mathematicians, scientists, and computing pioneers. Biography and historical setting lead each portrait, with science and mathematics explained in context.
assumed_background: Background varies by portrait; newer human-history entries are accessible without technical mathematics, while earlier manuscripts retain their own stated prerequisites.

editorial_policy: Lead with the historical person: family, education, places, work, institutions, relationships, political conditions and the sources that survive. Substantial mathematics and scientific reasoning are welcome in the spoken portrait, especially after the historical context is established; retain accurate worked examples instead of deleting them merely to satisfy a genre distinction. The main mathematical curriculum can carry the most systematic technical instruction. Evidence and material, not a fixed time, word count, chapter pattern, or biography-to-mathematics ratio, determine length and form. Keep historical claims source-grounded, distinguish memory and legend from contemporary evidence, and keep incomplete sketches in stubs/.
